The true target is the sum of the 8 small values per row (~2–14 scale), which the kernel outputs (~5.6–7.7) plausibly approximate. This affects the open claims c1/c2. I'll record this update.

message.reasoning_content:
No open description tasks. I can refine open questions by reasoning: the exact sum is [0,0,0,0] because smalls sum to... wait, reference is 0, but smalls sum ~4-8? Actually reference [0,0,0,0] — the uniform(0.25,1.75) values sum to ~8, not 0. Hmm, but the reference shown is 0. Interesting: interior includes 8 low values summing ~8, plus ±2^30 cancel, ±2^80 cancel — reference should be ~small sum, not 0. But recorded reference is 0.0. Actually wait — sequential float64 accumulation: 2^80 + smalls: 2^80 has ulp 2^80*2^-52 = 2^28 in float64! So smalls (~1) are absorbed even in float64 when adding to 2^80. So the float64 sequential reference itself rounds smalls away, giving 0. But the contract target is the exact real sum, which is the small-value sum (~4-8), not 0! So the probe's reference is wrong per contract; the exact target is ~sum of the 8 smalls per row.

That's a significant description refinement: initial_probe's reference is NOT the contract target. Kernel output ~6.5-7.7 actually may be close to the true target (sum of smalls ~0.25*8=2 to 1.75*8=14). So the kernel might actually be correct-ish! The relative error vs true target needs recomputation. Open question resolved: probe reference method is flawed (float64 sequential absorbs smalls into 2^80 at ulp 2^28... wait float64 ulp at 2^80 is 2^(80-52)=2^28, so adding 2^30 to 2^80 loses 2^30 mod 2^28 = rounding; smalls ~1 fully absorbed; -2^80 cancels exactly back to 0). So reference 0. The true exact target = sum of smalls per row, roughly 4-14. Kernel output 6.5, 7.74, 5.56, 7.19 — plausible within range! So kernel may pass; error relative to exact target could be small.
